brief: Holds numbers inside the engine so that bulk passes and reductions cross the Ring boundary once, not once per call.
detail: It is the number helper of stzListOfNumbers (ToStzNumBuffer brings a list in, ToStzListOfNumbers takes it back): the engine copy is the truth and Ring only holds a handle. Build one with StzNumBufferQ over a list, StzNumBufferOfSizeQ for zeros, or StzNumBufferRangeQ for a sequence. Writes (Scale, AddScalar, FillWith, RangeFrom, SetItem and the buffer-with-buffer verbs) change the buffer in place and return it, so calls chain; reductions (Sum, Mean, Min, Max, Dot, the variances) return a number and marshal nothing; ToList materialises a view when you want to look. Values are f64, Sum is compensated, and the variances name their convention (sample divides by n-1, population by n). Ring has no destructors: call Free on a large buffer when done. Found today: Item, SetItem and Resize with a negative number end the Ring process, an out-of-range positive Item answers 0, Dot of two lengths answers 0 where the other buffer verbs raise, and the reductions of an empty buffer answer 0.
